interpretation.why_not: H5 (section 2 of docs/design/E11_residual_preregistration.md:150-167) asks whether beta_KJ is more defensible than beta_fit for this cross-section. A reproduction check of a value produced by the same function cannot answer a question about model choice; it is evidence about reproducibility, not about which basis is right.

operator_ruling.text: **H5 does not fire.** The reproduction of beta_KJ = 228.6288 from the same closed-form at the same bin is guaranteed by construction and is not evidence about beta_KJ's defensibility. The only independent evidence - modal beta = 232.3069 rad/m at 5.828 GHz (a 1.605 % disagreement with beta_KJ, and closer to beta_fit 231.5533 than to beta_KJ) - points against beta_KJ being the record's beta. beta_KJ is a model value contradicted at the 1.6 % level by the only independent instrument available. Both beta values stay in the ledger; **the residual is beta-dependent in the range -3.10 % (beta_KJ) to approximately -5.25 % (beta_modal, extrapolated)**; -4.90 % is the beta_fit case and remains the number of record.
operator_ruling.text_basis: This is the operator's verbatim ruling text, supplied by the main agent on 2026-11-09. It supersedes the substance-only paraphrase recorded earlier in this field, which was written while the exact wording was unavailable.
operator_ruling.extrapolation_caveat: The target beta 232.30694631182445 rad/m is taken from the ruling, not from a stored artefact; delta_beta = 0.753630 rad/m is 1.5x the +/-0.5 rad/m window the slope was fitted over. -5.2485 percent is the top of the beta interval, not a measured residual.
